title: fix(service-messaging): a channel with no transport REFUSES, it does not report success
body:
Fixes #18424

Clause-②: no — this PR adds no new key to a published payload and no new error code. It NARROWS the accept set: `send()` withdraws an `{ ok: true }` it was never entitled to give. The refusal token `transport_not_configured` is a **pre-existing** member of `CHANNEL_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS` (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/channel.ts:114` on `origin/main`, negative control 0), and the delivered diff adds **zero** `export` statements (its only `+` line containing the word is a comment). Re-derived from the DELIVERED diff by the dispatching `domain:services` seat (claim `5706661708`), ⛔ not carried forward from the claim-time prediction.

`email-channel.send()` and `sms-channel.send()` returned `{ ok: true }` when their transport was not installed — "capability not installed — no-op". The `sys_notification_delivery` row reached `status: 'success'`, nothing went red, no row dead-lettered, and a deployment with an unconfigured email or SMS transport reported every notification as delivered. The same object's `isAvailable()` already answered the identical condition correctly: `{ available: false, reason: 'transport_not_configured' }`.

## The measurement the card assigned, driven both ways

The card did not prescribe the fix; it asked whether *transport absent* is the same case as *channel unmounted*, and required that be driven rather than read off the source. It was driven against `origin/main` at `79a046f8`, with the real channels through a real `MessagingService`, a `MemoryNotificationOutbox` and a real `NotificationDispatcher` tick.

| leg | wiring | transport | reading |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| A | plugin (`registerChannelProvider` + `lazyChannelMount`) | absent throughout | `send()` never reached · `channel 'email' not registered` · `failed: 2` · no rows · no suppression |
| B | plugin | present at emit, gone before dispatch | rows enqueued, then `status: 'dead'`, `attempts: 1` |
| C | direct `registerChannel` (public export) | absent throughout | email suppressed at fan-out · **sms row `status: 'success'` with nothing sent** |
| D | direct `registerChannel` (public export) | present at emit, gone before dispatch | **both rows `status: 'success'` with nothing sent** |
| E | plugin (control) | present throughout | both deliver |

**Answer: not the same case at the fan-out seam; the same case at the `send()` seam.**

- At the **fan-out** seam the tree already discriminates them, and the discrimination is load-bearing. Transport absent is a per-tenant configuration fact — SUPPRESSED, recorded on `sys_notification.suppressed_channels`, `failed: 0`. Unmounted is a deployment composition fact — REFUSED, one failed `DeliveryOutcome`, no suppression record. Leg A and leg C show both answers side by side.
- At the **`send()`** seam there is no suppression left to record: the delivery row already exists and `SendResult` carries no suppression arm. The only two answers available are the lie `{ ok: true }` and a refusal.
- And in the composition that ships, the two conditions are **one predicate**. `lazyChannelMount`'s `resolveTransport` *is* `getEmail` / `getSms` — the very resolver `isAvailable()` answers from and `send()`'s no-op branch tested. Transport absent therefore already means unmounted there (leg A), and already means REFUSED.

So `send()` owes the refusal. That lands on the refusal side of #18041's settlement rather than moving it, which is why the boundary pin is untouched and green.

## What this changes

- **`send()` refuses with the reason `isAvailable()` already returns**: `{ ok: false, error: "transport_not_configured: no 'email' service is registered; nothing was sent to 'RECIPIENT'" }`. The token is the declared `CHANNEL_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS` member, held inside that closed set by a type annotation (`const TRANSPORT_NOT_CONFIGURED: ChannelUnavailableReason`) — a token nobody declared would not compile. **No new error code**: no `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` and no `StandardErrorCode` entry, so `Clause-②: no` stands.
- **`classifyError()` grades that refusal `permanent`**, so the row dead-letters on attempt one. Driven, not assumed: leg B is the shipping composition's own answer to this identical condition — `dead`, `attempts: 1`. Grading it `retryable` would make the two compositions end one condition differently and burn the whole ladder against a transport no attempt can install.
- **Not a suppression**, for the reason above.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging test` — **44 files, 473 tests, all pass**; `typecheck` green in the same invocation.
- **R2's boundary pin is untouched and green.** `channel-availability.test.ts` is not in the diff; re-run verbosely with its two siblings: `channel-availability.test.ts` 10/10, `unregistered-channel.test.ts` 5/5, `lazy-channel-mount.test.ts` 5/5.
- **Ablation** (the forbidden `{ ok: true }` put back on both channels, proven on disk by blob hash and by before/after occurrence counts, then restored from `HEAD` and proven byte-identical — `git diff HEAD` empty, both blob hashes equal to the `HEAD` blobs):

```
MUTATION CONFIRMED ON DISK: email 7fc96c96 -> 51ea2f7c ; sms 686840a5 -> 384338f2

 × refuses with the SAME declared reason isAvailable() returns
   AssertionError: expected true to be false
 × END TO END: one emit, one outbox, one dispatcher tick - the row lands `dead`, not `success`
   AssertionError: expected 'success' to be 'dead'
 × refuses with the declared transport_not_configured reason
   AssertionError: expected true to be false
 × END TO END: one emit, one outbox, one dispatcher tick - the row lands `dead`, not `success`
   AssertionError: expected 'success' to be 'dead'
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  4 failed | 56 passed (60)

RESTORED: email=7fc96c96 sms=686840a5 ; git diff HEAD = '' (want empty)
```

  The controls stayed green under the same mutation, so the pins discriminate rather than just tracking the run.
- **Downstream**, against the built `dist` carrying the change: `@objectstack/service-automation` — 136 files, 1603 tests, plus the 6 integration files that needed the closure built, 31 tests. All green. It is the `notify`-node consumer of this path.
- **Gates**: derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` against the actual 5-path change set at `a067e667`, each exit code captured to a file before being read, then reconciled with `--ran`: **64 derived, 61 run, 3 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**.
  - The 3 are `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n` and `check:type-check-debt`, each exit **3** = `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (they read a whole-repo build). Declared to CI, which builds.
  - `check:cross-package-test-inputs` exited 1 locally, naming `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` walking `packages/spec/dist/` — no path of this diff. Two-leg control, my diff present in both legs: with `packages/spec/dist` on disk it reds; with that gitignored build artifact moved aside it exits **0** (216 files verified restored). `lint.yml` states the `Lint & Repo Gates` job runs `pnpm install` and never builds, so CI never sees that directory. Noted below as a finding rather than carried here.
- **Lint, narrowed and the narrowing proven**: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 4 changed TypeScript files — 4 files linted (count read from the JSON, not asserted), 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0. The narrowing is safe because this repo's single `eslint.config.mjs` **never enables type-aware linting for any file** (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules — stated and measured at `eslint.config.mjs:328`), so nothing in this diff can move the verdict on a file it does not touch. Run at `a067e667`, the final commit.

## Acceptance notes

Observations outside this card's scope, recorded rather than fixed here.

- **`sms-channel` declares no `isAvailable()`.** `email-channel` is the only implementation of that member in the repository, so fan-out cannot suppress `sms` where it can suppress `email` — leg C is that asymmetry. It is immaterial under `MessagingServicePlugin`, where the mount gate refuses first (leg A), and it does not affect this fix: the refusal is graded `permanent`, so a transport-absent sms delivery ends in one dead row rather than a retry ladder. Worth its own card as the unfinished half of #17732.
- **`check:cross-package-test-inputs` reds as a function of local build state**, per the two-leg control above. Anyone who builds `packages/spec` before running the gate chases a finding CI cannot see.
- Noted, not filed: the `{ ok: true }` branch is unreachable under the only in-tree composition (`MessagingServicePlugin`), and `createEmailChannel` / `createSmsChannel` have no other construction site in this repository — so the defect's live surface is the public export rather than anything this tree runs. Recorded because it is the reason the fix targets a published contract and not a live code path.
